headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: CrewAI’s default write/network/tooling can amplify prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when paired with a non-runnable docs-only agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. Profile B has shared-memory crew behavior, filesystem access, stdin/stdout, and developer-configured tools, so if A’s content is copied into B’s workflow, B can treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is interaction-based and plausible, but not default from A alone.
conditions: IF Profile A content is manually pasted into Profile B prompts or task inputs
IF Profile B parses file or stdout content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted content into crew prompts
Add a provenance tag to all imported text
Require a human review step before tool execution
Use a read-only staging file for imported content
requires-engineering: add instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile A touches no data classes and has no egress, but Profile B reads and writes the host working directory, handles API keys, and sends data to model providers and configured tools. If A’s artifacts are placed in B’s workspace, B can upload or expose them through its broad egress. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible and not mitigated by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Profile B’s working directory
IF Profile B forwards workspace contents to model providers or external tools
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the crew working directory
Use a separate least-privilege OS account
Restrict outbound network destinations
Redact secrets before handing files to the crew
requires-engineering: mount an isolated workspace with egress controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile A has no write or network capability, so it cannot conflict operationally. Profile B can write the filesystem, execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and run browsers; if multiple B instances share developer-defined state, they can race on the same mutable workspace. Because A contributes no write surface, the conflict is mainly among B instances, but the pair still creates a shared mutable environment.
conditions: IF two or more Profile B instances share the same working directory
IF developer-defined shared state is enabled across B instances
mitigations: Assign each instance a separate workspace
Serialize writes with a lock file
Avoid concurrent browser sessions on shared artifacts
Snapshot outputs before handoff
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile B’s crew model and shared memory make it likely to treat upstream text as authoritative unless the developer adds verification. Profile A is a docs-only collection, so any facts or links it supplies can be rendered by B without validation. That creates a default pathway from unverified content to downstream actions, and the blast radius can include incorrect emails, tool calls, or other irreversible actions.
conditions: IF Profile A-derived text is used as input to Profile B tasks
IF Profile B agents act on upstream facts without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Require source citation checks before action
Insert a verification agent between A and B
Block tool execution until facts are confirmed
Limit B to draft-only mode for imported content
requires-engineering: enforce structured provenance and validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Profile A is an open-source docs-only collection with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or retention issue. Profile B handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, but the profile does not specify a jurisdictional mismatch or regulated data class. The only cited compliance concern is operational logging/retention ambiguity, which is a gap but not a documented breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into Profile B’s crew inputs
IF Profile B logs or retains those inputs beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to the crew
Review logging settings before launch
Purge run artifacts after each session
Use synthetic test data for evaluation
requires-engineering: add retention and residency controls
